Synopsis:
A University of Southampton-led study finds that ship emissions — particularly from cruise vessels burning heavy fuel oil — generate ultrafine particles rich in vanadium and nickel that are more biologically harmful than road traffic pollution. The particles trigger lung cell inflammation and impair antiviral response. The port of Southampton serves 2.5M+ cruise passengers annually and sits upwind of a large urban population. Only ~15% of cruise ships currently use available shore power. The EU is moving toward mandating ultrafine particle monitoring around ports, a measure that does not apply to the UK post-Brexit.
